recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and do not add a duplicate core extension. Any future work on this artifact should be handled in the FHIR Extension Pack or DS4P Inline-sec-label guidance, with FHIR-44331 considered before reviving or changing the deprecated confidential extension.
issue_request: FHIR-26643 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested a standard extension on Address and ContactPoint to express the access policy associated with the element, using 0..* URI or CodeableConcept values with an example v3 ConfidentialityCode binding rather than a boolean confidential flag.
initial_application: A 2021 core commit mentioned FHIR-26643 while changing datatype extension spreadsheet sources, but the current core Address and ContactPoint extension spreadsheets do not contain a confidential/access-policy extension. The concrete application occurred in the FHIR Extension Pack: commit 370be10 and merge 743095c added StructureDefinition-confidential with Address and ContactPoint contexts, URI and CodeableConcept value choices, and the v3-Confidentiality example binding.
additional_context: Current core fhir.ini still includes datatype extension spreadsheet inputs, but the confidential extension definition is maintained in /home/jmandel/work/fhir-extensions. The current Extension Pack source marks that extension retired/deprecated and points implementers to Inline-sec-label. Later Published FHIR-44331 records the FHIR-I decision to deprecate the extension in favor of DS4P Inline-sec-label because it is generic, applies anywhere, and has implementation guidance. The related Zulip thread records Marc Duteau saying the FHIR-26643 fix would go into the extensions IG rather than base FHIR.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. The requested artifact belongs to the FHIR Extension Pack rather than the current FHIR core build, and the Extension Pack already contains the FHIR-26643 extension plus later deprecation guidance.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-I deprecated the FHIR Extension Pack confidential extension and pointed implementers to DS4P Inline-sec-label.
A later FHIR Extension Pack cleanup set experimental=false on this retired extension without changing the FHIR-26643 application decision.
